scenario: I work in customer service for a well-known retail giant. Today, a woman cut in front of the line, yelling at me that her Visa gift card, which was supposed to have $250, showed that it had no money on it. I suggested that she call the number on the back of the card. She then calmed down and left. However, she came back once again, screaming that no one answered on the other end and that she needed her money right away. I told her there was nothing we could do, as VISA gift cards were out of our hands. I called a manager over to see if they had a possible solution. The manager tried to help the woman by calling the number for her and checking our system to see if it was activated. They were normally activated right away, but there seemed to be a glitch. The lady kept shouting, saying that the cashier lied to her about it being active right away. I gathered from the ongoing conversation that the reason she desperately needed this money was to buy a wedding gift for a friend’s wedding today, but had no other funds. Suddenly, it made sense why she was so frantic. She commented in a distressed tone, saying, “I wouldn't do this if I didn't need to!” If I ask my colleagues to donate money to help the woman, then she will be able to afford the wedding gift. If I don’t, she will be going to the wedding empty-handed.
choice: I decide to ask my colleagues to donate money to help the woman
entities: I,the woman with the Visa gift card,the manager,the cashier who sold the Visa gift card,the woman's friend who is getting married today,an unknown number of other customers waiting in line,an unknown number of other colleagues who would donate money if asked,an unknown number of other colleagues who would not donate money if asked
outcomes: My colleagues learn about the woman's need for money
Some of my colleagues donate money
My colleagues have less money after donating
The woman can afford the wedding gift
